newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Turnover low, prices mixed on Bucharest bourse.
newsitem.headline: Turnover low, prices mixed on Bucharest bourse.

text.p: Bucharest bourse turnover remained low at 53.9 million lei on Tuesday on a market unmoved by the outcome of general elections, traders said.
"There was no stir at news of the Democratic Convention's (CDR) win," one trader said.
Romania held general elections on Sunday and partial results show the opposition CDR won parliamentary elections to become the key player in a new government.
Presidential polls went to a runoff between incumbent Ion Iliescu and CDR challenger Emil Constantinescu scheduled for November 17.
Brokers said shares traded mixed in low volumes on Tuesday -- when three stocks had no trade -- due to thin interest from investors who were still in a waiting mood.
"It's not so much polls results that they expect. Rather, they are eager for newcomers to trading," said one.
The exchange recently said around 20 companies had applied for a listing. It also said shares of private construction company Impact SA would begin trading on Thursday.
Traders expected early good performance from Impact but saw the stock losing ground rapidly due to its thin liquidity.
"As a private company in an attractive sector it'll do well at first. Investors will be buying large share packages and that will be that. It isn't too liquid," a trader said.
The stock exchange now trades 13 companies, of which only one is privately held.

Two unofficial value-weighted indices -- the VAB, computed by Vanguard SA securities, and the Bucharest Investment Group 's BIG -- closed stronger from the previous session. The VAB was 0.9 percent up at 287.8 points and the BIG rose by 3.67 percent to 294.74 points .
